holdout_selection: Before opening model results, select the first actionable snapshots of turns 2 and 4 in the latest encounter of each declared run that has both turns and passes the current raw-state schema. Record rejected encounters and never substitute cases based on model performance.
comparison: Same saved state and confirmed pre-cutoff memory; baseline versus frozen candidate with the same Jev model, two repetitions. No game commands or future observations in model input.
assessment: Inspect ordered energy, modifier use, current card identities, declared observation boundaries and preservation of existing benefits. A zero-damage X card can still have on-play value; do not impose a fixed strategy.
readiness: Known regressions must have correct causal facts and executable prefixes. Repeated historical decisions must not retain predictable stale-card continuations or systematic modifier-order losses; held-out cases must show no material mechanical regression. This establishes readiness for observed live play, not a victory guarantee.
limitations: Runs have historical development exposure. This is a prospective split for the sequence-dependency change, not a pristine benchmark. Previously inspected cases are regression examples, not fresh holdout evidence.
